data.title: Bitcoin price today: BTC below $64,000 as Citi cuts target to $99,532
data.description:
Bitcoin price today slipped further below $64,000 on Wednesday, November 18, after Citi cut its 12-month Bitcoin target to $99,532 and as US spot Bitcoin ETFs swung back to outflows ahead of the Federal Reserve's October minutes.

Bitcoin (BTC) traded at $63,465 on Coinbase at 15:08 UK time, down 2.2% from Tuesday's close of $64,873 at midnight UTC.

Citi cuts its 12-month Bitcoin and Ethereum targets

Citi cut its 12-month Bitcoin price target to $99,532 from $113,000 and its Ethereum target to $2,838 from $3,028, according to a research note reported by CNBC on Wednesday.

Citi analyst Alex Saunders said a rangebound crypto market had broken lower and that both assets had fallen since the bank's previous update.

He downgraded Citi's near-term outlook for capital inflows to neutral after Bitcoin dropped below its 200-day moving average.

Saunders pointed to weaker ETF demand, with Bitcoin fund flows in net outflow so far this year and Ethereum funds recording outflows in each of the past seven weeks.

Futures positioning pointed to broader deleveraging, he said, while a stronger US dollar, higher real yields and a rise in equity-market volatility had tightened the backdrop for crypto.

Bitcoin's correlation with the S&P 500 is again running above its correlation with gold, according to the note.

Citi had raised those targets to $113,000 and $3,028 in early October.

Even after the cut, the new Bitcoin target implies about 57% upside from Wednesday's Coinbase price. Ether traded at $1,769 on Coinbase, leaving about 60% implied upside to Citi's $2,838 Ethereum target.

What happened to Bitcoin price today?

Bitcoin traded between $63,001 and $64,933 on Coinbase on Wednesday, with sellers capping every move towards $65,000.

The world's largest cryptocurrency is about 16% below its November 9 high of $75,500 on Coinbase.

It hit $61,946 on Coinbase on November 15, its lowest point of the month so far.

The rest of the market was also lower. Ether traded at $1,769 on Coinbase, while XRP was at $0.98.

Why is Bitcoin price falling?

ETF demand has faded again, the same pressure Citi cited in its target cut.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $239.9 million on Tuesday, November 17, according to Farside Investors.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $209.5 million of that.

That reversed a small $7.9 million inflow on Monday.

Since October 30, the funds have lost about $3.2 billion in 13 sessions, based on Farside's daily data.

US spot Ether ETFs lost $29.1 million on Tuesday, Farside data show.

Interest rates are the other weight.

The Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on October 28, but Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voted for a quarter-point hike.

On Tuesday, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy "will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027", in remarks in Argentina.

Higher rates make non-yielding assets like Bitcoin less attractive.

The US dollar index touched a 52-week high of 103.91 on Wednesday, according to TradingView.

What happens next?

The Fed's minutes from its October 27-28 meeting are due at 19:00 UK time on Wednesday.

Traders will look at how many officials backed a hike and how soon. The Fed's next decision is on December 9.

Bitfinex analysts said in their Bitfinex Alpha report on Monday that they expect Bitcoin to trade between $61,800 and $69,400 this week, with another test of the November 15 low possible.

They named $57,803, Bitcoin's July cycle low, as a key level to watch, and said a recovery above $72,700 with renewed ETF inflows would show selling pressure is fading.

Farside's figures for Wednesday's ETF flows will show whether institutional selling has eased.

Should you buy Bitcoin now?

Bitcoin has held above last week's low, but ETF outflows and a hawkish Fed are still weighing on it.

Citi's reduced 12-month target of $99,532 still sits well above the current price, though that is a forecast, not a recommendation.

A hawkish set of minutes could push Bitcoin back towards $62,000, while a softer tone could bring buyers back.

For more coverage, see our latest cryptocurrency news.

data.title: AI reputation management after a hack: why engines skip your incident report
data.description:
AI engines quote the page that holds the claim they are writing, and after a hack, that is rarely your own post-mortem.

Ledger published its response to the CryptoBilis implant attack on 15 October.

By the next morning, ChatGPT was quoting it, while Google still did not show it.

That morning, we asked four AI engines 10 questions about the incident, and Ledger's post appeared as a source in 5 of the 40 answers. The other 35 did not cite it.

An engine treats your incident report as one source among many and cites it only when it holds the exact claim the answer needs.

AI reputation management after a hack starts with writing those claims into the page.

A hack ends in a week. AI keeps telling the story for months.

This column is part of Crisis Memory, ICODA's November series on what ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini say about crypto brands after a crisis, with insights from Vlad Pivnev, Anastasia Marmuzevich, Anastasia Shalepina and Artyom Abbasov.

Did AI quote Ledger's post-mortem?

Only partly: ChatGPT cited the 15 October post in 4 of its 10 answers, Perplexity in 1 of 10, and Claude and Gemini never did.

ChatGPT sent 24 of its 34 citations to Ledger's own sites, including the 2020 breach notice and the 2023 Connect Kit report.

Claude sent 1 of its 52 there and built its answers from BleepingComputer, Help Net Security, The Hacker News and Bitquery.

Perplexity cited 232 sources across its 10 answers, and Ledger's post appeared in one of them.

Gemini skipped web search in 6 of its 10 answers, and none of those answers mentioned the incident.

How do AI engines pick a source after a hack?

An engine cites the page that contains the claim it is writing, so every claim your post-mortem leaves out gets sourced from someone else.

Ledger's answers show that rule in three claims.

In the second row, Claude gave Bitquery's $102.0M across 324 wallets and Specter's $86M+, then added: "Ledger itself said it has not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost."

In the third row, the post is dated 15 October and mentions no earlier statement, although Ledger had spoken on 9 October and confirmed the implant on 10 October.

Does a Google ranking mean AI search visibility?

No: on 16 October, ChatGPT quoted Ledger's post while Google did not show it, so rank and AI search visibility need separate tracking.

For the query "ledger hack", an old phishing-campaigns page still held #2, and the 15 October response was missing. Engines run their own retrieval, so a page can be quoted before it ranks.

Google's AI Overviews diverged by market too: after the news broke, they vanished from brand queries such as "ledger" in the US, UK, France and Germany, and stayed in Malaysia and Indonesia, where they cited crisis coverage within one to three days.

"First hours, nobody recalls statement quality; they remember search results," said Anastasia Marmuzevich, Head of PR at ICODA.

Old pages compete with the new one. ChatGPT cited Ledger's 2020 breach notice and 2023 incident report next to the new post.

In the Crisis Memory prompts about Ledger, the 2020 leak appeared in 25 of 48 answers and the 2026 implant in 15.

What should an incident page contain so AI quotes it?

Write the page as a set of claims an engine can lift: dated milestones, confirmed numbers, who is affected and what users got back.

  • Date every milestone: the first statement, the confirmation, and each update. A page that shows one date hands the engine that date.
  • State what is confirmed and what is not, with numbers where you have them. Without them, engines fill the gap with Specter's $86M and Bitquery's $102M.
  • Put the recovery in the same paragraph as the hack. In our Crisis Memory data, recovery came up in 33 of 34 Bitget answers that mention the hack, 30 of 38 for Bybit, and 11 of 45 for Kelp DAO.
  • Turn the questions people ask into headings, such as "Were users compensated?" and "Is the device safe to use?", and answer each in the first sentence.
  • Get one independent outlet to repeat your facts: 51 of Claude's 52 citations went to third-party sites.
  • Check all four engines in the first week, because answers barely move afterwards. When we repeated the audit 24 days later, only 2 of 40 carried news from after 16 October.

"Treat the incident page as an answer sheet: every question an engine might get about the hack should have a dated, quotable answer on it," Anastasia Shalepina, AI SEO Expert, ICODA.

Method: API versions of ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini with web search, US location, one run per prompt, 16 October 2026. Crisis Memory covers 296 answers across five crypto brands.

🔍 Check if AI cites your brand → https://icoda.io/ai-visibility/

data.title: Why Micron stock is falling despite strong Nvidia results?
data.description:
Micron Technology MU shares fell in early trading on Wednesday as investors remained cautious about the broader fallout from Nvidia's leadership crisis, even after the chip giant delivered strong quarterly results.

Micron was down around 0.88% at 10:06 AM ET, trading near $707. The decline came after the stock had gained in after-hours trading following Nvidia's earnings report on Tuesday.

The weakness reflected lingering concerns across the artificial intelligence trade, with peer Sandisk also falling in early trading.

Nvidia shares also traded lower during Wednesday's session despite forecasting fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion and reporting third-quarter sales of $115.8 billion, comfortably above analyst expectations.

Nvidia results could help Micron

Nvidia's latest results included a significant increase in its supply commitments, which rose to $390 billion from $279 billion in the previous quarter.

The company said the commitments were primarily related to multi-year procurement of memory supply, potentially providing a boost to manufacturers such as Micron that are expanding production of high-bandwidth memory (HBM).

HBM chips are a critical component of AI infrastructure, enabling processors to access large volumes of data at high speeds.

Micron is one of the key suppliers seeking to benefit from rising demand for these specialized memory products.

However, the market response suggested that strong demand forecasts alone were not enough to ease concerns about the risks surrounding the AI infrastructure buildout.

Nvidia leadership uncertainty continues to weigh on sentiment

The controversy surrounding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure has added another layer of uncertainty to the AI trade.

Huang had offered to return to the role if the board determined that his reinstatement would be in the company's best interest.

However, Nvidia's board rejected the proposal and said it would proceed with a search for a permanent successor.

Investors are now watching whether the leadership transition could affect Nvidia's strategy, particularly its aggressive investment and financing arrangements supporting AI infrastructure customers.

The broader market backdrop has also remained challenging for semiconductor stocks, with investors questioning whether AI-related capital spending can maintain its pace amid regulatory, political and financing concerns.

RBC reiterates Buy rating on Micron with $1,500 target

Despite the pressure on the stock, RBC Capital Markets maintained a bullish stance on Micron.

Analyst Srini Pajjuri reiterated a Buy rating and a $1,500 price target on Tuesday. The target stands well above Micron's recent trading range of around $700.

Pajjuri has highlighted Micron's positioning in high-bandwidth memory, the prospect of firmer pricing and tighter industry supply-demand conditions as factors that could support earnings growth.

Broader Wall Street sentiment also remains positive.

Data from Google Finance showed 28 Buy ratings and one Hold among 29 analysts covering Micron, with an average price target of approximately $1,624.

Micron's next earnings report, expected in December, should provide investors with a clearer picture of demand for its memory products, pricing trends and the company's ability to capitalize on AI infrastructure spending.

Until then, the stock could remain sensitive to developments surrounding Nvidia and broader sentiment toward AI-related investment.

data.title: Google stock analysis: may benefit from Anthropic IPO but major risks remain
data.description:
Google stock has plunged and moved into a bear market after falling by over 30% from the year-to-date high. GOOG was trading at $277, down sharply from a high of $403. This retreat may continue as the company continues to face major headwinds. 

Google to benefit from Anthropic IPO, but gains may be short-lived

Alphabet is set to be one of the biggest beneficiaries of Anthropic’s IPO, which is scheduled for today. Google has emerged as one of the company’s largest investors, holding a 14% stake. 

If Anthropic debuts at a $1.5 trillion valuation, that stake would be worth $210 billion, a substantial return on an investment of less than $10 billion. The value would climb even higher if the stock jumps after the listing.

Alphabet was also one of the biggest beneficiaries of SpaceX’s IPO since it is now its biggest investor. The company owns 555 million shares, currently valued at $78 billion. At its peak after the IPO, this stake was worth over $124 billion. 

The risk, however, Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic will start falling if the stock trades as other newly listed companies. For example, SpaceX stock initially surged after the IPO and then dropped by over 50% within a few days. Other recent IPOs like Circle Internet Group, Medline, Figma, and Klarna have all plunged after the IPO. 

Alphabet’s business is facing headwinds and tailwinds

The most recent results showed that Alphabet’s business is facing headwinds and tailwinds. On the positive side, the company’s cloud revenue is soaring as demand from AI companies surge. Its revenue soared by 103% in the third quarter, driven by AI infrastructure. 

The company’s Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon have seen substantial growth, with the Gemini app having over 1 billion downloads. Its models are processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, app by 40% from the second quarter. 

On the other hand, however, there are signs that its AI investments are cannibalizing its core business. Google Search made over $63 billion in the third quarter, while YouTube Ads, Google Network, and subscriptions, platforms and devices grew by 9%, 1%, and 11%, respectively. TPU, its chips are also doing well.

The challenge, however, is that the company is spending aggressively in its business. Its capex jumped to over $51.35 billion last quarter, up from $44 billion in the second quarter. As a result, the company has started burning cash. Its free cash flow stood at negative $9 billion, a big reversal after making over $24 billion in the same period last year. It has burned over $14 billion in the last two quarters. 

The company has also continued raising cash. It recently raised $80 billion to raise cash, including from Berkshire Hathaway. It also recently raised $3.8 billion in Hong Kong. 

These fears explain why analysts have slashed their targets for the stock. UBS Group slashed its target from $380 to $320, while Wells Fargo reduced the target to $365. Other analysts who slashed their targets after earnings are from BMO, Cantor Fitzgerald, Piper Sandler, and Scotiabank.

Google stock technical analysis

GOOG stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the GOOG stock has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months. It has dropped from $403 to the current $277. It gapped lower after the recent earnings report.

The current price is along the 50% Fibonacci Retracement level. It has also slumped below the 50-day moving average and the Supertrend indicator. 

Therefore, there are signs that the stock is in an overall bear market, which may continue in the coming months. In the long term, however, the stock will likely bounce back.

data.title: Anthropic stock price targets: what analysts say before the ANT debut
data.description:
Wall Street's largest banks will not be publishing Anthropic price targets tonight, because the firms underwriting the IPO are in a research quiet period. That has left a small group of independent houses to put numbers on the stock before Class A shares in the Claude developer are due to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, 19 November, under the ticker ANT.

The figures sit well above the official $70–$78 range in Amendment No. 3 to Anthropic's Form S-1, filed on 17 November, and above $80, the level at which the Wall Street Journal has reported Anthropic expects to price, citing people familiar with the matter.

That report is not a new filing, and the official range has not changed. Two of the targets reached the public via secondary reports and should be treated as individual views, not a settled Street forecast.

What are the Anthropic stock price targets so far?

The highest 12-month target in circulation is $105, from New Street Research. Analyst Pierre Ferragu initiated coverage with a Buy rating, CNBC reported on 17 November, calling Anthropic a "generational IPO".

He argued that AI would take a growing share of spending on knowledge work, spreading twice as fast as cloud computing did after 2010, across an addressable market 10 times larger, and that the IPO was being priced "on the cautious side". Reuters, citing the same note, said New Street expects revenue of $505 billion by 2030, from $53 billion in 2026 — New Street's projections, not company guidance. We looked at the initiation in more detail when the Buy rating was published.

Freedom Finance, part of Freedom Broker, has a Buy rating and a $101.90 target, according to a note seen by Oninvest on 13 November.

Analyst Alem Bektemirov tied the valuation to further growth in large enterprise customers. Oninvest is a secondary source.

KGI Securities initiated coverage with an Outperform rating on 16 November, StreetInsider reported, naming analyst Zheng Jiemao.

Investing.com reported the accompanying target as $100 a share. That figure also comes via a secondary report.

Morningstar is working from a different kind of number. In an 11 November note, analyst Malik Ahmed Khan, CFA, set a base-case fair-value estimate of $92.00 a share, equal to $1.7 trillion in equity value on his figures.

He described Anthropic as a narrow-moat company and said the $70–$78 IPO range, which he put at up to $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted share count, reflected souring sentiment towards AI rather than the firm's fundamentals.

He saw about 24% upside from the midpoint and viewed the stock as undervalued in that range, with a bull case of $188 and a bear case of $25. The $92 figure is a fair-value estimate, not a 12-month Street target.

Seaport Research Partners has not put a target on the stock. It initiated coverage on 7 November, before the price range was filed, but deferred a rating and a target until after the IPO, according to Investing.com. That report also cited a Seaport discounted-cash-flow valuation of about $1.64 trillion, which is not a published price target and predates the filed range.

How much upside do those numbers imply?

From the $78 top of the official range, New Street's $105 target implies about 35% upside, Freedom's $101.90 about 31%, KGI's $100 about 28%, and Morningstar's $92 fair value about 18%. From the $74 midpoint, those figures are about 42%, 38%, 35% and 24%.

From $70, New Street's target implies 50% upside. If the deal prices above $80, as the Journal has reported, the same four figures would imply about 31%, 27%, 25% and 15%. A sharp jump on Thursday would narrow the gap further for anyone buying in the open market rather than in the IPO.

Why have the underwriting banks not published targets?

Because they are in a research quiet period. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the representatives of the underwriters, according to the prospectus.

Under FINRA Rule 2241, firms that participated in an IPO of a company that is not an emerging growth company are generally barred from publishing research about the issuer for 10 calendar days after the offering date. The older 25-day research blackout no longer applies. A broader set of bulge-bracket targets is therefore unlikely in the first days of trading. Seaport has said it will return with a rating and a target after the IPO.

The views already out are clustered, and they are all constructive at the $70–$78 range. They do not remove the risks in the prospectus, including large compute commitments and a history of GAAP losses.

Anthropic reported a net loss of $104.0 billion for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, including $94.3 billion of fair-value changes on convertible notes and related instruments.

📅 We are tracking the price, the valuation and the research as it appears on our Anthropic IPO date, valuation and ticker hub.

data.title: Why is Nvidia stock falling over 2% on Wednesday?
data.description:
Nvidia shares NVDA fell 2.2% on Wednesday, extending their decline to a fifth consecutive session, as the US House Committee on Energy and Commerce demanded a formal briefing from the chipmaker over alleged export control violations and former CEO Jensen Huang's reported links to a suspected Chinese spy.

Representative Brett Guthrie, chairman of the committee, sent a letter to Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress requesting that company officials appear before lawmakers no later than December 2.

The inquiry focuses on whether Nvidia circumvented federal restrictions intended to prevent advanced artificial intelligence technology from reaching China.

Lawmakers are also examining allegations that a senior company official attempted to interfere with a federal investigation.

The developments add to the pressure on Nvidia as it navigates a leadership transition and scrutiny over national security concerns, despite strong quarterly results and an upbeat revenue outlook.

Congressional probe focuses on export control allegations

In his letter, Guthrie said the reported events raised questions about Nvidia's compliance with federal export laws and the effectiveness of its security controls.

The congressional investigation centres on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer suspected of helping Chinese companies circumvent US export restrictions.

On November 16, the Justice Department and Commerce Department publicly confirmed a joint criminal investigation into the company.

Reports have also linked Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is alleged to have a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, to suspected Chinese intelligence activities.

According to Guthrie's letter, investigators are examining claims that she established a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia hardware.

Lawmakers are also looking into allegations that the Commerce Department transferred its initial investigation into Megaspeed to the Justice Department last year after Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce officials seeking information about the inquiry.

These allegations have not been established as findings of wrongdoing by Nvidia.

Leadership transition adds to investor concerns

The controversy has coincided with significant changes at Nvidia's senior leadership level.

On November 8, Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital affair in an internal email to employees and said the company's board had launched an independent investigation into national security concerns raised by media reports.

Four days later, he announced his departure from company leadership.

Kress, Nvidia's former chief financial officer, took over as interim CEO while the company works with an external firm to find a permanent replacement.

The uncertainty has weighed on investor sentiment, with Nvidia shares declining for five consecutive trading sessions and facing the prospect of a seventh consecutive weekly loss.

However, Wall Street analysts have pointed to the company's latest financial results as evidence that demand for AI infrastructure remains strong.

Nvidia reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share, beating analyst expectations by 21 cents.

Revenue reached $115.84 billion, up 103.2% from a year earlier and $7.13 billion above forecasts.

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, compared with analyst estimates of $124.89 billion.

The forecast assumes no data centre computing revenue from China.

Analysts remain positive on Nvidia's outlook

Several Wall Street firms have maintained positive views on Nvidia despite the leadership uncertainty.

RBC reiterated its Outperform rating, citing demand that continues to exceed supply, a product roadmap extending over the next three years and limited near-term competitive risks due to industry supply constraints.

The firm also highlighted rising supply purchase commitments as evidence of strong demand visibility.

Morgan Stanley maintained its Overweight rating, pointing to strong demand for AI computing and Nvidia's competitive position.

Its analysts also viewed the company's willingness to provide forward-looking commentary as a positive.

Wedbush raised its price target to $293 from $275 while retaining an Outperform rating.

The firm said Nvidia's near- and medium-term demand outlook remained unchanged despite Huang's departure.

The company also has $227.3 billion remaining under its share buyback authorisation.

Kress described returning capital to shareholders as a top priority during the earnings call and said Nvidia could fully utilise the remaining authorisation by fiscal 2028.

Jefferies said the buyback programme offered another potential source of support for the stock, while noting that investors still need greater visibility into the company's strategic direction following the leadership transition.

Meanwhile, Kress said Nvidia was raising its fiscal 2028 outlook and expected revenue growth of approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% previously and on a higher fiscal 2027 base.

data.title: Nvidia earnings: investors still need answers to two key questions
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) more than doubled its quarterly revenue to nearly $116 billion in its fiscal Q3 and issued impressive guidance for the future as well.

But buying NVDA shares this morning means betting on growth that still has to be earned. Two questions matter for that bet:

  1. Can Nvidia keep delivering new chips on schedule and winning big orders without Jensen Huang?
  2. If tighter US rules choke off Chinese demand served through Singapore, can it turn those same chips into just as much profit somewhere else?

Nvidia stock is currently down nearly 35% versus its year-to-date high.

Key man risk remains alive for Nvidia stock

While the media narrative this morning is how Nvidia earnings essentially silence the “key man” risk, it’s worth noting that the company’s quarter ended Oct. 25 – about two weeks before its board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation.

Simply put, Huang ran Nvidia for the entire quarter.

So, the earnings beat, and even the guidance, tells investors that orders Nvidia had already secured translated into strong sales. The real test for interim CEO Colette Kress and NVDA stock actually begins with the “next round of orders.”

Kress told CNBC that key cloud customers were still asking for more computing power.

The harder question is whether those customers will keep committing billions to Nvidia’s next generation of chips.

A delayed launch or a large order that goes elsewhere could dent future earnings, turning investors less willing to pay a premium for each dollar Nvidia earns.

China remains a key overhang on NVDA shares

A chip can sit in a Singapore data centre and still do work for a customer in China – the new US rules target some of that remote access.

Nvidia recorded $11.05 billion, about 9.5% of quarterly sales, from direct customers headquartered in China and Hong Kong.

Its print leaves the amount of Chinese demand served through Singapore unknown.

On CNBC, Jim Cramer asked whether other buyers could absorb chips Nvidia might stop shipping to the region without pushing prices down.

Kress explained how Nvidia checks who will use the chips and whether data centres are ready.

But she gave no indication of how quickly alternative buyers could take delivery or whether they would pay the same price.

That remains a key overhang on Nvidia shares.

Technical setup warrants caution on Nvidia

Even from a technical perspective, NVDA shares have not turned attractive yet.

The AI darling currently sits firmly below major moving averages (MAs), with an RSI in the early 20s indicating intense selling pressure.

That said, Wall Street hasn’t thrown in the towel on Nvidia yet.

The consensus rating on the chip-maker remains at Strong Buy, with the mean price target of about $258 indicating massive upside potential from current levels.

data.title: DJT stock is at a record low: Why Trump Media could fall to $2 or lower
data.description:
Trump Media stock has remained under pressure this week and is hovering near its all-time low. DJT traded at $4 on Wednesday, down more than 70% so far this year. The sell-off may continue through the rest of the year, and there is a risk that the stock could fall below $2 over the longer term.

Trump Media faces a $1 billion debt wall

Trump Media, the parent company of Truth Social, is facing some major risks. One of them is that the company needs to repay about $1 billion by November 30. 

The debt emerged from the company’s decision to invest in Bitcoin, mirroring the strategy that Michael Saylor perfected at Strategy. 

It issued that debt in May last year. According to its prospectus, the debt matures on May 29 2028, but its holders can demand cash repayment on November 30th. The stock remains much lower than its conversion price, meaning that cash repayment is more attractive than converting. 

The company is now in a bind as it does not have that money in its balance sheet. As a result, the options include selling its Bitcoin holdings, which are now valued at about $1 billion. It can also decide to raise cash by selling shares, a move that will dilute its shareholders. Also, it can use some of its cash to repay the debt.

These challenges are compounded by the ongoing deterioration of Bitcoin and other coins. Bitcoin dropped to $63,857, down by 27% from its highest point in October. It has also dropped by nearly 50% from its highest point in October last year. At its all-time high, its Bitcoin holdings were worth about $2 billion. 

Trump Media is facing other challenges

The company is facing other risks. For example, Democrats recently won the Senate and the House of Representatives, and will most likely investigate the company for its Truth+ product. This is a service that lets people and companies pay about $100,000 a month to get access to Truth posts from the most active users on its platform. This service is widely seen as a way for Trump to monetize the presidency. 

Further, Trump’s approval rating has continued falling after the midterm elections. This rating stands at 31%, the lowest point of both of his terms, and the trend may continue since he is not working to end the Iran war. As a result, with the president’s popularity fading, there is a likelihood that traffic to the website will also drop. Indeed, SimilarWeb data shows that the traffic dropped by over 22% in October.

Trump Media has a narrow path for making real profits. Its last earnings report showed that its net profit rose to over $409 million from a loss of $238 million in the previous quarter. However, most of these profits came from its Bitcoin gains, which have now reversed.

Further, in the long term, it is hard to imagine how the company survives, especially when Trump leaves office.

DJT stock price technical analysis

Trump Media stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the DJT stock has been in a strong sell-off in the past few months and is now at its all-time low. It has already dropped below the important support level of $6.96, its lowest level on June 25. 

The stock remains below all moving averages and the Ichimoku cloud, a sign that bears remain in control. Also, the Relative Strength Index (RSI) and the MACD have continued moving downwards. 

Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling as its fundamentals deteriorate. In the long term, this decline may hit $2 and below.

data.title: Why is gold price down today? Gold futures slip 2.5% to September 2025 low
data.description:
US gold futures slipped on Wednesday to their lowest level since September 2025, as hawkish Federal Reserve comments and a stronger dollar hit the non-yielding metal.

COMEX gold futures for December delivery were down $96.00, or 2.48%, at $3,768.20 an ounce at 13:21 UK time.

The contract hit a session low of $3,744.60, down 3.1% from Tuesday's price.

Spot gold was down 2.04% at $3,770.65 at 13:21 UK time after touching $3,742.71.

What happened to gold price today?

December futures traded near $3,857 on Tuesday, fell below $3,800 before 03:00 UK time and slid again shortly before 13:00 UK time, COMEX data via TradingView showed.

The low took the contract below Monday's previous 52-week low of $3,835.20 and left front-month gold futures about a third below their 52-week high of $5,626.80, set on January 29.

The selling spread across precious metals.

COMEX silver futures for December delivery were down 3.43% at $45.735 an ounce, according to COMEX data.

Why is gold price falling?

The main driver is the Fed. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said on Tuesday that the US likely needs several more rate hikes, in remarks at the Central Bank of Argentina.

“The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve price stability in a timely manner,” Musalem said.

New York Fed President John Williams told Axios that the AI boom could argue for further rate increases, though he did not see a need for “dramatic action”.

Higher rates raise the opportunity cost of holding gold, which pays no interest.

The US 10-year Treasury yield stood at 5.115%. The Fed's target range is 3.75% to 4%.

The dollar added to the pressure.

The US dollar index rose 0.16% to 103.77 after touching 103.91, a 52-week high, according to TradingView.

A firmer dollar makes bullion expensive for buyers using other currencies. The dollar also hit a 19-month high last week.

What happens next?

Minutes from the Fed's October 27-28 meeting are due at 19:00 UK time on Wednesday.

A hawkish tone could keep the dollar and yields elevated. For gold, the next test is whether futures can hold above Wednesday's $3,744.60 low.

Should you buy gold now?

Gold is falling as markets price in higher US rates, and the downtrend has not yet turned.

Despite the near-term concern, Goldman Sachs sees the precious metal reaching $4650 by the end of 2027.

If investors are confused between buying bullion, a gold ETF or mining stocks, you can read this guide on how to invest in gold to learn about the ways you can invest and the opportunities and risks that prospective investors should know.

Tonight's Fed minutes will show whether the hawkish shift behind gold's slide has further to run.

data.title: Nasdaq rises as Nvidia forecast lifts stocks; Anthropic IPO in focus
data.description:
US stocks opened higher on Wednesday as Nvidia’s stronger-than-expected revenue forecast eased concerns about the chipmaker and lifted sentiment across stocks.

Investors were also looking ahead to the pricing of Anthropic’s initial public offering, which could provide an important test of demand for companies linked to the AI boom.

Nvidia shares rose 1.6% in trading after the company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.

That was above the average analyst estimate of $125.25 billion, according to LSEG data.

The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.35% while the S&P 500 rose 0.13%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 210 points.

Nvidia forecast boosts chipmakers and AI stocks

Nvidia’s outlook helped ease investor concerns following the sudden departure of former CEO Jensen Huang last week.

Uncertainty surrounding the company's leadership and future prospects had weighed on confidence in the AI trade.

The company's board dismissed the possibility of rehiring Huang on Tuesday, despite a campaign calling for his return.

Its latest revenue forecast nevertheless provided reassurance about its near-term business outlook.

Companies involved in AI infrastructure reversed premarket gains after the market opened.

Neocloud providers CoreWeave and Nebius fell 5.4% and 0.79%, respectively.

Data centre-related firms IREN and Applied Digital fell between 0.25% and 2.4%.

Nvidia's shares could remain under scrutiny as investors assess developments following Huang's exit.

The company's latest forecast has helped restore some confidence, but uncertainty around its leadership remains a factor for the stock.

Anthropic IPO pricing in focus

With Nvidia's results out of the way, attention is shifting to Anthropic's IPO pricing later on Wednesday.

The creator of the Claude chatbot is targeting a valuation of as much as $1.4 trillion.

The offering would mark the first-ever IPO by a frontier AI model developer and provide an indication of Wall Street's appetite for businesses at the centre of the artificial intelligence boom.

The timing makes the listing particularly significant for technology investors.

Nvidia's forecast has reinforced expectations for continued demand in the AI sector, while Anthropic's proposed valuation will test how much investors are willing to pay for a leading AI model developer.

Fed policy and other stocks in focus

Monetary policy was another major focus for markets.

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said on Wednesday that the central bank should either raise interest rates by 50 basis points at its December meeting or signal a more aggressive response to inflation.

Investors were also awaiting the minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee's October meeting, due later on Wednesday, for further clues about the policy outlook.

Traders were almost fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate increase next month, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Several Federal Reserve officials had called for more aggressive rate increases following a hotter-than-expected October inflation report.

Among individual stocks, Lowe's fell 1% in trading after forecasting annual profit below Wall Street expectations, despite raising its sales outlook.

Target gained 4% following its quarterly results.

Take-Two Interactive moved in the opposite direction, gaining 6.1% as the global rollout of its Grand Theft Auto VI video game began.
